activity.notes: The Union of Lublin was concluded on 1 July 1569 and created the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth with a common monarch. Sigismund II Augustus remained its monarch until his death on 7 July 1572. ATLAS begins this Commonwealth Activity with the creation of the real union in 1569; it does not retroactively label his earlier Polish and Lithuanian rulership as rule of the Commonwealth.

sources.title: Union of Lublin
sources.citation_text: The Central Archives of Historical Records describes the exchange of union acts and oaths on 1 July 1569 and the king's confirmation of the Union on 4 July.

sources.title: Sigismund II Augustus
sources.citation_text: The Encyclopedia of the Early Modern World identifies Sigismund II Augustus as the last Jagiellon king and treats the permanent Polish-Lithuanian Union of 1569 as the central constitutional achievement of his reign.
